findings.title: Frequency, ECL110 displace and heat-curve offset hold the cycle's step through the next step
findings.claim: The writes cut from the cycle's action (compressor frequency, ECL110 MQTT displace on both topics, the heat-curve offset entity) are never re-derived at a plan-step boundary, so with the default 30-min cycle over 15-min steps the command in force is another step's in 45-57 % of graded minutes on the reference plant.
findings.mechanism: `_current_action` is cut once per solve (async_run_optimization -> get_current_action) and `_command_frequency` (via `_commanded_split`), `async_publish_current_action` -> `heat_curve.publish` and the valve hold schedule read it only inside `_async_update_data`; the supply (`pump_arbiter.supply_tick`, #2492) and the arbiter's one-minute tick re-derive their step each minute, these do not. A cycle whose tail lands after the boundary (cell 3478) writes the step it was cut for into the next one.

findings.phenomenon_property: Every actuator write whose value is a function of the plan step is re-derived at each plan-step boundary (within the arbiter's one-minute tick), not only when the cycle runs.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator write tail: re-cut the action's step-dependent fields (or the action) at each plan-step boundary from the same one-minute step tick that drives the supply, and run the frequency/MQTT/curve/valve writes from it, keeping their own rate limits.

findings.title: Disinfection switch is commanded from the previous solve's action, one interval late
findings.claim: The pump's disinfection switch turns on one cycle after the steps the plan books the anti-legionella cycle on: for a 06:30-07:00 window it is on 0 of 30 minutes inside the window and 30 minutes after it, and the space-only steps of the window stay in Heating mode (0 of 30 minutes Heating + DHW).
findings.mechanism: `LegionellaGuard.async_track_cycle` (reached from `_update_current_state` -> `async_observe`, the first thing `_async_update_data` does) reads `self._action()`, the action the previous solve cut; the solve that adopts this step's legionella action runs after it, so the switch and the arbiter's `inp.disinfecting` (DisinfectionSwitch.memo) follow one interval behind, and the switch is not re-driven between cycles.

findings.title: A switch-on leads no mode when the arbiter's stale record matches the step's mode
findings.claim: When the mode select changes while the supply reads off (the pump's own reset, a person) and the arbiter's record still holds the step's mode, the switch-on of a partial step lands with the hot-water mode in force; Heating follows one tick later.
findings.mechanism: `_lead_mode` (#3420) calls `_write`, which returns early when `held.written['mode']` equals the target; `hold()`, which drops a record the entity no longer reads, never runs while the switch reads off (`_arbitrate` returns at `_pump_off`), so the record is stale exactly when the lead is needed.

findings.title: Floor-level space steps short-cycle where the floor lift exceeds min lift plus stop hysteresis
findings.claim: Under a pump with an integrating speed loop and a 2 K stop hysteresis, a step booked at the modulation floor (min-cold-tank, 1.0 kW) runs 30 starts in 2.5 h at 0.60 kW on a plant lifting 8 K/kW (38 starts, 0.50 kW at 10 K/kW) against the plan's one run at 1.0 kW; the power-feedback loop never corrects it.
findings.mechanism: The floor writes inlet + flow_min_lift_k (5 K); a pump whose water at its floor sits higher than that plus its stop hysteresis stops and restarts. `_feedback` resets its run on every stop and folds only running samples, so its windowed error is 0 (running at the floor = the booked floor) and `_nudged` stays in the deadband; the duty-cycle shortfall is never seen.

leads.what: With the clock past the last step the loop's else-branch returns the last step's action (heat_pump_on included); cycle_supply falls back to it where step_supply gives None, so the baseline state's supply value is the last step's, not a handed-back pump (M2 value of the baseline row).

Without dhw_hysteresis_entity the plan books hot-water charges on a tank inside the pump's start band; the arbiter writes the configured set-point and 0 kWh is delivered (effect.py dhw_only_tank47_ent0), the ledger reading idle-instead rather than not-startable.

Every reload writes the baseline row (Heating + DHW) and restores the space set-point baseline (35 C), then the new instance rewrites the plan's row at its first solve (cells.py restart: writes at minutes 34-36): a restore per reload, M6's once-rule to check.
